'''Sean M. Decatur''' (born September 4, 1968) is an American chemist and college administrator who has served as the president of the [[American Museum of Natural History]] since April 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/12/06/arts/design/natural-history-museum-sean-decatur.html|title=Natural History Museum Names College Leader as New Chief
|last=Pogrebin|first=Robin|date=Dec 6, 2022|work=New York Times|access-date=6 December 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=American Museum of Natural History Names New President | website=US News & World Report | date=December 6, 2022 | url=//www.usnews.com/news/best-states/new-york/articles/2022-12-06/american-museum-of-natural-history-names-new-president | access-date=April 6, 2023}}</ref> Decatur is the first African-American to serve as the museum's president. Prior to this, he was president of [[Kenyon College]] from 2013 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-12-08|title=Decatur to Step Down, Will Lead Natural History Museum|url=https://kenyoncollegian.com/news/2022/12/decatur-to-step-down-will-lead-natural-history-museum/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=The Kenyon Collegian|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Decatur is a native of the [[Cleveland]], Ohio, area. His mother was a public school teacher of mathematics and science. He attended Cleveland public schools and the [[Hawken School]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.kenyon.edu/about-kenyon/office-of-the-president/biography-2/|title=Biography|website=www.kenyon.edu|publisher=[[Kenyon College]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141009014653/https://www.kenyon.edu/about-kenyon/office-of-the-president/biography-2/|archive-date=October 9, 2014}}</ref>  He earned a [[bachelor's degree]] at [[Swarthmore College]] in 1990 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[biophysical chemistry]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1995.<ref name="bio"/>

==Career==
Decatur taught at [[Mount Holyoke College]] from 1995 to 2008. He served as an assistant professor of chemistry, then an associate professor of chemistry, and served as department chair from 2001 to 2004. In 2005, he was appointed the Marilyn Dawson Sarles Professor of Life Sciences. He was also an associate dean of faculty for science from 2005 to 2008.<ref name = "bio" />

Decatur was a visiting scientist at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 2004 to 2005. From 2008 to 2013, he served as dean of the College of Arts and Sciences at [[Oberlin College]]. In 2013, he was named president of [[Kenyon College]].<ref name="Farkas">{{cite news|url=http://www.cleveland.com/metro/index.ssf/2013/05/sean_decatur_cleveland_native.html|title=Sean Decatur, Cleveland native and Oberlin College dean, is new president of Kenyon College|last=Farkas|first=Karen|date=May 6, 2013|work=Cleveland Plain Dealer|access-date=17 August 2014}}</ref>

During his final years at Kenyon College, Decatur faced challenges related both to labor organizing and [[transgender]] rights.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-12-08|title=Staff Editorial: Thank You, President Decatur|url=https://kenyoncollegian.com/opinion/2022/12/staff-editorial-thank-you-president-decatur/=2023-01-25|website=The Kenyon Collegian|language=en}}</ref> From 2020 to 2022, students expressed concern over the college not recognizing a student worker labor union.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-04-15|title=Undergraduates Across the Country Are Unionizing College Workforces|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/labor-student-unions-kenyon-college-dartmouth-wesleyan-grinnell/=2023-01-25|website=CBS News|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2023-02-14|title=Kenyon Student Workers Are Unionizing. They Say the College Is Fighting Them.|url=https://jacobin.com/2023/02/kenyon-college-student-worker-union-organizing-nlrb-labor-law=2023-05-21|website=Jacobin|language=en}}</ref> In 2022, students demanded that the college publicly support a transgender staff member, [[Rhea Debussy]], who was receiving transphobic threats. When a statement was not issued, students delivered a list of demands to Decatur's office.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-03-08|title=Kenyon College Students Deliver a List of Demands to College President to Address Transphobia and Transmisogyny|url=https://thebuckeyeflame.com/2022/03/08/kenyon-college-student-deliver-demands/|access-date=2023-01-26|website=The Buckeye Flame|language=en}}</ref> Following this, a transgender student then wrote an open letter to Decatur and the college community.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-04-06|title=In Response to Kenyon's President: What Trans Folks Need on TDOV and All Year Round
|url=https://thebuckeyeflame.com/2022/04/06/in-response-to-kenyons-president/|access-date=2023-01-26|website=The Buckeye Flame|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Decatur is married to Renee Romano, professor of history and Comparative American studies at [[Oberlin College]].<ref name="Farkas" /> They have two children, Sabine and Owen.
